groups.text: It is currently a clear morning in Berlin-Tempelhof with a temperature of 24 degrees.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Anthropic is integrating its own browser directly into the Claude Cowork desktop app. This allows the AI to open a side panel where it can load pages, click buttons, and type to fill out forms or extract data from dashboards that lack an API. To maintain privacy, this browser remains separate from the user's personal tabs, bookmarks, and passwords. Users may move logins over one page at a time from Firefox, Edge, or Chrome, though banking and email sites remain off-limits. For pages already open and signed into, users must still rely on the Chrome extension. Anthropic warns that prompt injection risks exist and advises users to stick to trusted websites. The feature rolls out this week for Enterprise customers and those on Pro, Max, and Team plans.

Ukrainian forces have targeted the warehouses of Russian e-commerce giant Ozon in Ufa and Orenburg. The company reports that while its Orenburg facility has already resumed operations, the logistics complex in Ufa remains closed for inspection following minor damage. This follows a strike on August 22 that destroyed an Ozon warehouse in Samara Oblast, as Ukraine continues a campaign against Russian retail infrastructure. Meanwhile, Russia is leveraging internal Ukrainian friction through disinformation. The firing of popular Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov sparked street protests and calls for wartime elections, which the Kremlin has exploited with fabricated claims to portray the Ukrainian government as illegitimate. In a separate part of Europe, record low river levels caused by drought are changing the landscape in northern Bulgaria. Along the dried-up banks of the Danube, volunteers are searching for fossils and artifacts after receding waters revealed mammoth bones this past July.

In France, the focus shifts this Thursday to the economy as main candidates for next year's presidential election face a grilling by business leaders. At the Medef employers federation's annual end of summer conference, these candidates will be questioned on taxation, reindustrialisation, the burden of regulations, and a public debt that now exceeds 3.5 trillion euros. While political figures navigate national debt, Amazon subsidiary Ring is addressing privacy concerns for its connected cameras and doorbells. Starting in September, the company will deploy a new default encryption called TAKE, or Throw Away the Key Encryption, to limit server access to video keys. This move aims to strengthen confidentiality without fully sacrificing cloud processing functions. Users will soon choose between this new standard and end-to-end encryption, which offers total privacy but blocks features like video search and descriptions.

Artificial intelligence is now embedded in the tools you use every day, often working quietly in the background. It is the technology that allows your phone to recognize your face and enables map applications to suggest traffic detours. Banks also rely on these systems to identify and block suspicious purchases. Unlike traditional software that follows rigid rules written by humans, modern AI uses machine learning to identify patterns from examples. This shift allows machines to perform tasks once reserved for people, such as understanding phrases or predicting behaviors. While the concept of thinking machines dates back to the 1950s, three factors have caused a recent explosion in capability. These include a massive increase in available data from the internet and a significant rise in processing power through specialized video cards. Together, these elements have turned AI into one of the most important technologies of this generation.

In Shillong, the Khasi Students’ Union has temporarily suspended its agitation following a meeting with Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma. The union expressed some satisfaction after discussing five key demands from a twenty-point charter, including migrant worker registration and the proposed Shree Cement project. While the group is pausing its protests, fifteen issues remain unresolved for future discussions. This local political tension in Meghalaya contrasts with the systemic environmental crisis in Assam. Official data shows that between 2012 and 2022, floods in Assam claimed one thousand two hundred fifteen lives and caused over four hundred billion rupees in damages. The disaster affected more than two point five million hectares of cropland during that decade. While the state has built some four hundred twenty-three embankments covering over four thousand eight hundred kilometers, critics argue these structures fail to address the deeper governance gaps driving the cycle of devastation.

France's effort to block minors from adult content is showing a significant gap between law and practice one year after the SREN law's age verification requirements took effect. While the obligation for pornographic sites to verify users became the rule on July 15, 2025, following a Council of State decision, new data suggests the measure is largely ineffective. An Ifop survey conducted in July 2026 found that consumption has simply shifted toward platforms that ignore the law. Specifically, 78 percent of minors and 69 percent of adults who viewed pornography in the last year did so on sites that do not require age verification. The tension is clear: nearly half of adult users and 65 percent of minors stopped using compliant sites entirely to avoid the checks. Ultimately, 36 percent of respondents now use only non-compliant sites, while just 23 percent stick exclusively to those following the law.

India is planning to expand its merchant fleet by 100 ships over the next five years to reduce its reliance on foreign shipping lines. Union Minister of State for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Shantanu Thakur noted that India currently spends roughly 75 billion dollars annually with foreign firms to move essential cargoes like coal, crude oil, natural gas, and urea. However, Indian ship owners report it is 16 to 20 percent more expensive to operate under the Indian flag due to freight taxes, higher financing costs, and taxes on maintenance and imports. To address this, the National Shipping Board has proposed a five-point plan focusing on tax reforms, affordable financing, and simplified regulations. In other news, cybersecurity experts warn that AI-driven security is failing because it relies on logs and events that are lossy representations of reality. Current systems often filter out 80 to 90 percent of telemetry before it reaches security monitors, leaving AI models without the complete data needed to detect complex attacks.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with rain chances up to 43 percent and temperatures between 23 and 27 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: birthday: Antonia Kokalj turns 15 and birthday: Felix Möller turns 41, at 14:00, Meeting Aaron, at 16:00, AutoML Seminar, and at 19:00, ️ Greifen and ️ Greifen.
Mail worth checking: Songkick about Just announced: Jason Moran and Laura from Bolt about When it’s time to head out.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
